name: DNA damage response → cell-cycle arrest
summary: DNA damage activates the sensor kinases ATM (double-strand breaks) and ATR (single-stranded DNA / replication stress). They activate CHK2/CHK1 and stabilise p53. p53 induces p21, which inhibits CDKs so RB stays active and the cell arrests in G1; CHK1/2 also inhibit CDC25, blocking CDK activation. If damage is irreparable, p53 induces apoptosis.
clinical: Checkpoint loss (TP53, ATM mutation) lets cells with damaged DNA keep dividing — a hallmark of cancer. PARP, ATR and WEE1 inhibitors exploit DNA-repair defects in tumours.

references.label: Jackson & Bartek (2009) Nature 461:1071 — The DNA-damage response

nodes.label: DNA damage
nodes.description: Double-strand breaks (ionising radiation) or stalled forks (UV, replication stress).

edges.description: CDK activity is required for progression; inhibiting CDKs causes arrest.

steps.title: 1 · Damage is detected
steps.text: Double-strand breaks recruit the MRN complex, which activates ATM. Single-stranded DNA coated with RPA recruits ATR–ATRIP.

steps.title: 2 · Checkpoint kinases
steps.text: ATM phosphorylates CHK2; ATR phosphorylates CHK1. These spread the signal through the nucleus.

steps.title: 3 · p53 is stabilised
steps.text: ATM and CHK2 phosphorylate p53 near its MDM2-binding site (Ser15, Ser20). MDM2 can no longer tag p53 for degradation, so p53 accumulates.

steps.title: 4 · p21 blocks CDKs
steps.text: p53 activates the CDKN1A gene. p21 protein binds and inhibits cyclin–CDK2 complexes. Meanwhile CHK1/2 inactivate CDC25, so CDKs keep their inhibitory phosphates.

steps.title: 5 · Arrest — or death
steps.text: Without CDK activity RB stays bound to E2F and the cell cannot enter S phase (or mitosis) until repair is complete. If damage is irreparable, sustained p53 induces PUMA, NOXA and BAX, triggering apoptosis.
